newsitem.title: CHINA: Hopewell says sells remaining CEPA stake.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell says sells remaining CEPA stake.

text.p: Hopewell Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it has agreed to sell the remaining 19.99 percent stake in Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd to SEI Holdings, a subsidiary of Southern Company, in exchange for CEPA's 80 percent interest in a Java power plant project and US$150 million cash.

Hopewell said in a statement it would transfer its 266.47 million shares in CEPA to Southern, which in turn would transfer CEPA's 80 percent interest in the Tanjung Jati coal fired thermal power plant project in Central Java, Indonesia to Hopewell and pay US$150 million in cash.
Southern Co completed an acquisition of an 80 percent stake in CEPA from Hopewell and other CEPA shareholders in January.

Hopewell said the deal valued its stake in CEPA at around HK$5 billion. The two parties agreed on a price of HK$15 per CEPA share and about HK$3.9 billion for CEPA's stake in the Java power plant, it said.

"The transfer of the CEPA shares will give rise to an exceptional gain to the group," Hopewell said. "It is expected that the short term reduction in recurrent earnings from the CEPA shares will be offset by longer term recurrent income from the TJB (Tanjung Jati) project, whilst the transaction is not expected to have a material adverse impact on the working capital of the group."
Hopewell said the US$150 million would be used as general working capital, including requirements related to the Java power plant.
Hopewell said Gordon Wu would step down as chairman of CEPA but would remain a member of the board.
After the deal, Southern Energy Inc, a subsidiary of Southern Co, will own more than 99.9 percent of CEPA.
The Java power plant project, Tanjung Jati B, is a 1,320 MW coal-fired power station in Indonesia, which should be constructed on a build-operate-own basis.
Hopewell said construction began in 1996 and is forecast to be completed in the year 2000.

The estimated total cost of the project is about US$1.77 billion, of which about US$440 million is expected to be financed by equity, of which US$244 million has been invested to date, and about US$1.33 billion by project financing.
Hopewell said on completion of the transaction, it would have control over the construction, development and operation of the Java project.
Trading in Hopewell shares was suspended on Tuesday and was due to resume on Wednesday. The stock last traded at HK$5.10.
